title: Izmail corridor (P0784/P0786/P0787) — three distinct pipelines; P0784 is a Frankenstein row needing rewrite, not deletion

rows.recommendation: Do NOT delete. ШДКРІ (Shebelinka-Dnipropetrovsk-Kryvyi Rih-Izmail) is a real, independently-confirmed pipeline distinct from both P0786 (ATI) and P0787 (RI) — it needs a REWRITE, not removal. (1) Drop the fabricated 'Rozdilna' waypoint from the name — no source anywhere calls this line by that compound name; Rozdilna is P0787's own line, not a waypoint on this one. (2) Replace Capacity 24.00 bcm/y: this traces, confirmed verbatim by fetching GEM's own cited academic source directly, to a table row aggregating THREE physical threads (ATI + ШДКРІ's two threads) into one combined CIS-border-crossing throughput figure — it is not this line's own capacity, and using it here double-counts capacity that P0786 (ATI) already carries on its own row. Research a standalone figure before pasting one of the two candidates found (Moldovatransgaz's own per-thread reading of 7.3 bcm/y at 820mm for the line's Moldovan-transiting portion, vs. the Ukrainian-wiki-sourced combined ШДКРІ+RI figure of up to 15.8 bcm/y — note this second figure is ШДКРІ+RI TOGETHER, not ШДКРІ alone, so it is not a clean substitute either). (3) Treat Length 164.00 km as unconfirmed for the full Shebelinka-to-Izmail route: GEM's own cited source (ngpedia.ru) attaches 164 km to a sub-designation 'Shebelinka-Krivoy Rog-Izmail II' of uncertain scope (one thread? one segment?), and independently, the merged route geometry draws a 759.1 km schematic lower bound for this corridor (route_geometry_findings.md finding B) — 164 km cannot be the whole line's length. (4) Diameter 1200mm has the most solid direct sourcing of the four fields — a live, reachable ProZorro capital-repair tender for this exact pipeline gives DN1200 at km 108.5-111 near its Shebelinka-area origin — but the same trunk tapers to ~800-820mm by the time it reaches the Balkan-bound outlet near Izmail (per Moldovatransgaz's 820mm reading of the transiting tail and the Ukrainian wiki's 'two threads of 800mm' at 1975 commissioning); note the tapering diameter in ResearcherNotes rather than treating either figure as simply wrong.
rows.notes: GEM's own outbound citations for this exact wiki page (read under standing rule 4 — for outbound cites only, never cited here as a source) trace each of P0784's four data fields to a DIFFERENT, unrelated origin — the signature of a Frankenstein row, not a duplicate: Capacity 24 -> cyberleninka.ru (Gainutdinova); Length 164km -> ngpedia.ru; Diameter 1200mm -> a ProZorro tender; Name -> an apparent fusion of ШДКРІ's real corridor with 'Rozdilna', a waypoint that belongs to a different line (P0787). I fetched the cyberleninka article directly and confirmed the exact table row verbatim: «Ананьев - Тирасполь - Измаил, Шебелинка - Измаил (три нитки) | 24 | Румыния, Болгария, Греция, Турция, Македония» under Table 1, 'Пропускная способность экспортных газопроводов в пунктах пересечения западной границы стран СНГ' (capacity of export pipelines at CIS western-border crossing points) — an aggregate across three physical threads, not P0784's own line. I independently fetched Ukrainian Wikipedia's dedicated Shebelinka-Izmail corridor article and confirmed verbatim: 'трубопровід Роздільна — Ізмаїл діаметром 820 мм, постачання по якому розпочали у жовтні 1973 року' (Rozdilna-Izmail, 820mm, deliveries from October 1973) and, on ШДКРІ, 'Введений у дію у 1975 році, він мав дві нитки діаметром 800 мм. Разом газопроводи ШДКРІ та Роздільна — Ізмаїл могли забезпечувати постачання на Балкани в обсягах до 15,8 млрд м3 на рік' (commissioned 1975, two 800mm threads; TOGETHER with Rozdilna-Izmail, up to 15.8 bcm/y combined — note this figure is the two lines COMBINED, not ШДКРІ alone). The same article lists five real component systems of this corridor: Shebelinka-Dnipropetrovsk, ШДО, ШДО-2, Rozdilna-Izmail, and ШДКРІ. Two ProZorro tenders (one GEM's own citation, one independently surfaced by search, both confirmed reachable at HTTP 200 via direct curl) corroborate a DN1200 capital-repair scope on this pipeline's Shebelinka-area segment (km 108.5-111) — the page bodies are client-rendered JS and unreadable directly, so this is reachability-confirmed, not full-text-confirmed; documented as an access limitation, not treated as fabricated. ngpedia.ru (source of the 164 km figure) was unreachable both live (TLS cert mismatch) and via Wayback (503) — recorded as unreachable, not as a deletion signal. Independently of all the above, Tiraspoltransgaz's own blog (ttg-pmr.livejournal.com) documents ШДКРІ undergoing a joint magnetic-tomography diagnostic inspection with Russian specialists as its OWN separate maintenance program, distinct from Rozdilna-Izmail's separately-documented 2012-13 repair work — independent operational confirmation that these are two really-separate assets despite sharing an 820mm/7.3bcm spec pair (the Soviet parallel-strings pattern the brief warned about). Independent route geometry (route_geometry_findings.md, finding B) also corroborates that 164km cannot be right: the merged 5-vertex schematic for this row spans 759.1 km end to end, a 4.6x gap even as a lower bound.

rows.recommendation: Not a duplicate of P0784 or P0787 — keep the row, Anan'iv-Tiraspol-Izmail (ATI) is real and correctly named. But flag StartYear1 for correction/verification: GEM has 1968; Ukrainian Wikipedia's dedicated ATI article (8 references) instead dates commissioning to 1986, with a further capacity expansion completed by ~2001 that raised the line to its stated 20 bcm/y max. No source found in this pass supports 1968 for this line specifically. Independently, Tiraspoltransgaz's own corporate history page places ATI's pipeline + associated turbine-driven compressor-station construction (Tiraspol/Orlovka/Ananyev/Tarutino) in its 1983 entry, with earlier entries (1965-71) describing only the region's pre-existing gas-distribution infrastructure and a 1975 ELECTRIC (not turbine) compressor station — consistent with a mid-1980s completion, not 1968. Also flag Capacity 23.70 bcm/y against the sourced ~20 bcm/y post-expansion maximum (Moldovatransgaz gives 20 bcm/y directly) — close but not identical, worth a dedicated Update check; Diameter 1200mm (sheet) vs 1220mm (Moldovatransgaz) is immaterial rounding.
rows.notes: Moldovatransgaz's own asset register (item 4 of 8) names «Ананьев - Тирасполь - Измаил (АТИ)» as its own separate line: 62.91 km (Moldovan portion), 1220mm, 20 bcm/y. Ukrainian Wikipedia's dedicated ATI article independently gives 1200mm diameter, 1986 commissioning, and a post-expansion max of 20 bcm/y ('її завершення дозволило збільшити максимальну пропускну здатність газопроводу на 4 млрд м3 у рік, завдяки чому вона досягла 20 млрд м3'). Existence and the ATI name/acronym are further corroborated, independently of both wiki sources, by direct coverage of the 1 April 2009 Transnistria pipeline explosion: Kommersant (Tiraspol-area location, pipe age >30yr, blast-crater detail) and realitatea.net, which names the line explicitly as 'Ananiev-Tiraspol-Izmail (ATI) magistrale' with a 127.5km damaged section repaired by 9 April 2009; RT's coverage of the same event calls it 'Ananiev-Odessa-Izmail', a name variant for the same event/line. Four independent sources (Moldovatransgaz, Ukrainian wiki, Tiraspoltransgaz's own corporate history, and 2009-explosion press coverage) converge on this being its own distinct, separately-named, separately-dated trunk — refuting any duplicate reading against P0784 or P0787.

rows.recommendation: Not a duplicate of P0784 or P0786 — keep the row. Diameter (820mm) and Capacity (7.30 bcm/y) both match Moldovatransgaz's own per-line asset figures for «Раздельная - Измаил (РИ)» exactly; no change needed there. Do flag/verify StartYear1: GEM has 1975, identical to ШДКРІ's own commissioning year (suspicious echoing, possibly copied across rows) — Ukrainian Wikipedia's corridor article instead dates Rozdilna-Izmail deliveries to October 1973, two years earlier and sourced separately from ШДКРІ's 1975. Recommend a targeted Update check against a primary Ukrtransgaz/TSOU construction chronology (source-ladder item 2) to settle this rather than rely on secondary wiki sourcing alone.
rows.notes: Moldovatransgaz's asset register (item 2 of 8) gives «Раздельная - Измаил (РИ)»: 92.24 km (Moldovan portion), 820mm, 7.3 bcm/y — diameter and capacity match GEM's P0787 exactly; GEM's 230km full length is not contradicted since Moldovatransgaz's figure is explicitly the Moldovan-territory portion only, and route_geometry_findings.md's 193.3km drawn schematic is an unremarkable lower bound. Ukrainian Wikipedia independently dates Rozdilna-Izmail deliveries from October 1973, DISTINCT from ШДКРІ's 1975 commissioning two years later — exactly the kind of independently-sourced, separately-dated-commissioning evidence the briefing's Kazakh precedent treats as dispositive against a duplicate reading, despite RI and ШДКРІ sharing an identical 820mm/7.3bcm/y spec pair. Tiraspoltransgaz's own blog independently corroborates RI undergoing its own separate 2012-13 repair/maintenance program, distinct from ШДКРІ's separately-documented joint diagnostic inspection — confirming these are two really-separate, independently-operated assets (the Soviet parallel-strings pattern), not the same pipe recorded twice under P0787 and P0784.

summary:
P0784, P0786 and P0787 are three physically distinct pipelines in the Izmail transit corridor, not one line triple-counted — the redundancy hypothesis is REFUTED as a whole-row duplicate/deletion question. Moldovatransgaz's own trunk-line asset register (the pivot source) lists Rozdilna-Izmail (RI) and Shebelinka-Dnipropetrovsk-Kryvyi Rih-Izmail (ШДКРІ) as two separate numbered line items with two different Moldovan-portion lengths (92.24km vs 91.817km) despite an identical diameter/capacity pair (820mm/7.3bcm/y) — the documented Soviet-era parallel-strings pattern, confirmed independently by Tiraspoltransgaz's own blog showing the two lines under separate, unrelated maintenance programs. Ananiiv-Tyraspol-Izmail (ATI) is listed separately again with its own spec (1220mm/20bcm/y, 62.91km), and its existence/naming is independently corroborated four ways: Moldovatransgaz, Ukrainian Wikipedia's dedicated ATI article (1986 commissioning, 8 references), Tiraspoltransgaz's own corporate history (construction 'at a rapid pace' in 1983), and three independent press accounts of the 1 April 2009 Transnistria pipeline explosion on this exact line.

However, P0784 as GEM currently records it IS a genuine data-quality problem — just not a duplicate-count one. Reading GEM's own outbound citations for the P0784 wiki page (permitted under standing rule 4: read gem.wiki for its outbound cites, never cite gem.wiki itself) shows each of its four fields traces to a DIFFERENT, unrelated source — a Frankenstein row. The name fuses ШДКРІ's real corridor with 'Rozdilna', a waypoint belonging to a different line (no source calls this line by that compound name). The capacity (24bcm/y) traces — confirmed verbatim by fetching the cited academic article directly — to a table titled 'capacity of export pipelines at CIS western-border crossing points' that explicitly aggregates THREE physical threads (ATI plus ШДКРІ's two threads) into one figure, not P0784's own throughput; using it here silently double-counts capacity P0786 (ATI) already carries on its own row. The length (164km) traces to an unreachable encyclopedia page describing an ambiguous sub-designation, and independently, merged route geometry draws a 759.1km schematic lower bound for this corridor — 164km cannot be the full line's length regardless of that source's fate. The diameter (1200mm) is the one field with solid, independently-corroborated sourcing (a live, reachable ProZorro capital-repair tender for this exact pipeline's Shebelinka-area segment), though the same trunk plausibly tapers to ~800-820mm by its Balkan-bound outlet.

The recommendation is REWRITE, not delete: ШДКРІ is real and deserves a correctly-specified row (drop 'Rozdilna' from the name; replace the borrowed aggregate capacity with a properly-researched standalone figure — neither of the two candidates found is a clean substitute; flag length as unconfirmed pending further research; keep the diameter with a tapering note). P0786 and P0787 need smaller fixes: P0786's StartYear1 (GEM: 1968) conflicts with two converging independent sources dating commissioning to 1986 (Ukrainian wiki + Tiraspoltransgaz's own corporate history), and P0787's StartYear1 (GEM: 1975, suspiciously identical to ШДКРІ's own year) conflicts with the corridor wiki's October 1973 date specifically for Rozdilna-Izmail — both worth a targeted Update pass against a primary Ukrtransgaz/TSOU chronology, neither an existence or duplicate question. Verdict is PARTIAL_OVERLAP rather than a clean REFUTED because the capacity VALUE on P0784, unlike the row itself, genuinely does double-count throughput already recorded on P0786.
open_questions: What is ШДКРІ's correct standalone (non-aggregate) capacity figure for a rewritten P0784 — Moldovatransgaz's per-line reading of 7.3bcm/y (one thread, transiting portion) or some other figure? The wiki's 15.8bcm/y is ШДКРІ+RI combined, not a clean substitute either.

What does the 164km figure attached to 'Shebelinka-Krivoy Rog-Izmail II' actually measure (one thread, one construction-stage segment, or something else)? ngpedia.ru was unreachable both live and via Wayback; needs a fresh access attempt or an alternate source quoting the same figure with more context.

Is there a primary Ukrtransgaz/TSOU construction chronology (source-ladder item 2) that can settle P0786's 1968-vs-1986 and P0787's 1975-vs-1973 start-year discrepancies with one authoritative document, rather than the secondary wiki/corporate-history sourcing used here?

Does GEM need a genuinely NEW row for ШДКРІ if P0784 is renamed/rewritten to represent it, or does the existing P0784 ProjectID simply get corrected in place — an Update-workflow implementation question, not a redundancy-adjudication one.
